title: SurfaceGui
summary: GUI painted onto a part's face: shop screens, keypads, wall posters with buttons. Sized in studs relative to the part face.

properties.name: Face
properties.description: Which face of the part (Front, Back, Top…).

properties.name: Adornee
properties.description: The part it renders on (defaults to Parent).

properties.name: PixelsPerStud
properties.description: Resolution density: gui pixels per world stud (default 50).

properties.name: Enabled / Active
properties.description: Visibility and interactivity (buttons on the surface).

explanation.whatItIs: A GUI texture-mapped onto a part face — a working screen inside the 3D world, buttons included.
explanation.whyItExists: Diegetic UI: TVs, vending machines, door panels — interfaces that belong IN the scene.
whenToUse: Any UI that should live on a surface
tips: PixelsPerStud controls sharpness — bump it for readable text on big walls
Buttons on a SurfaceGui work with clicks (raycast-based input) — test on mobile
Anchor the part or the surface moves with physics
commonMistakes: Wrong Face — the UI renders on the back of the wall
Expecting interaction through walls — input needs line of sight

examples.title: Wall-mounted button panel
examples.code:
local wall = workspace.KeypadWall

local surface = Instance.new("SurfaceGui")
surface.Face = Enum.NormalId.Front
surface.Parent = wall

local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.25)
button.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.25, 0.3)
button.Text = "OPEN DOOR"
button.Parent = surface

button.Activated:Connect(function()
    print("Door button pressed")
end)
